title: Bank Jateng Borobudur Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Borobudur Marathon 2026 Review | Magelang, Central Java
meta_description: Borobudur Marathon review: a course record of 2:17:33 on 16 November 2025, a Kenyan sweep, World Athletics Elite status, and friendly crowds in Magelang.
dek: The marathon around Borobudur temple was upgraded to World Athletics Elite status for 2025, and the course record fell. Here is what the November 2025 edition was like.
verdict: The Bank Jateng Borobudur Marathon is Indonesia's temple marathon, run in Magelang regency around Borobudur, and in 2025 it was fast. On Sunday 16 November 2025, Kenya's Ezra Kipchumba won in 2:17:33, the fastest time in the race's history, breaking the 2:19:35 set in 2019 [1]. Kenyans filled all eight prize places in the men's marathon and six of eight in the women's [1]. The race had just been upgraded from a World Athletics Label to Elite status [1]. The winner said the weather was warm but suited his race plan, and praised the friendly residents cheering along the roads [1]. If you want a World Athletics Elite marathon in Southeast Asia with a remarkable setting, it is a top choice.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: The race was held in Magelang regency, Central Java, on Sunday 16 November 2025 [1]. It is organised with the Central Java provincial government, Bank Jateng, the Kompas daily and the Borobudur Marathon Foundation [1].
For 2025 the race was upgraded from a World Athletics Label to Elite status, which raised its prestige and prize money and requires the organisers to invite elite runners [1].

sections.heading: A Record at the Front
paragraphs: Ezra Kipchumba of Kenya won the men's marathon in 2:17:33, ahead of Alex Oloitiptip Korio (2:17:43) and Kiprop Tanui (2:18:01) [1]. Kipchumba's time was the fastest ever at the race, beating Geoffrey Birgen's 2:19:35 from 2019, and it earned him Rp 250 million [1]. The fourth-placed runner, Edwin Cheruiyot Soi, is a 2008 Olympic 5,000 m bronze medallist [1].
Kenyan runners took all eight prize places in the men's marathon and six of the eight in the women's [1].

sections.heading: What the Winner Said
paragraphs: Kipchumba, running Borobudur for the first time, said he was very happy to win [1]. He described the weather on the day as warm but good for his strategy, and said the support of the residents along the roadside lifted him: friendly people, and he enjoyed competing in Indonesia [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a marathon with an elite international field in the Borobudur area of Central Java.
Plan for warmth and humidity in mid-November in Central Java, and for crowds: the roadside support is part of the appeal.

This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition. Kompas, which published the report used here, is one of the race's organisers. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: Who won the Borobudur Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: Kenya's Ezra Kipchumba won the men's marathon on 16 November 2025 in 2:17:33, the fastest time in the race's history, ahead of Alex Oloitiptip Korio and Kiprop Tanui. Kenyans took all eight prize places in the men's marathon and six of eight in the women's.

faqs.question: Is the Borobudur Marathon a World Athletics race?
faqs.answer: Yes. For 2025 it was upgraded from a World Athletics Label to Elite status, which increased its prize money and requires the organisers to invite elite runners. The men's winner received Rp 250 million.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Borobudur Marathon?
faqs.answer: Warm. The 2025 winner described the race-day weather as warm but good for his strategy. Mid-November in Central Java is hot and humid, so most runners should pace for conditions.
